summary.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.name: Specialized winding wires (incl. CTC)
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue in FY26 and FY25; grew 62% in FY26 and 103% YoY in Q4. CTC is the majority of specialized wires; management does not disclose CTC volumes. Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard wires.

segments.name: Standard winding wires
segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue grew 92% YoY (after 37% in Q3 and 22% in Q2). Exports were about 27% of revenue in Q4 (excluding other operating revenue) and all go to T&D customers in four continents.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected to be at least the FY26 rate of 21%, as full-year Supa capacity is available.
Sustainable EBITDA per ton range of about 65,000-74,000 (earlier commentary: 67,000-74,000); actual depends on product mix and export share.
Next tranche of new capacity (Supa) expected to come online around Q2 FY27; Supa completion on track for FY27, taking installed capacity to about 59,000 MT.
Green copper backward integration facility expected to commence in H2 FY27.
Payable days targeted above 25 days and close to 30 days by end FY27; working capital days expected to trend lower over the next several quarters.
Operating leverage from new capacity expected to kick in gradually after Q4 FY27; fixed costs of new capacity will persist through FY27.
PEEK insulated wire capacity expected online around end of Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution 1.5-2 years out.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at March 31, 2026 was 43,445 MT; Supa Phase II expansion takes it to about 59,000 MT, with completion targeted for FY27.
Consolidated utilization was about 70% in Q4 FY26; peak utilization is planned at about 85% of installed capacity, which takes 2-3 years to reach for a new plant.
Around 65% of current installed capacity is for specialized wires and the balance for standard wires.
Space exists for another 10,000 MT at the Supa site (land, building and some utilities already in place); no decision yet.
3.2 MW rooftop solar commissioned at Supa in May 2026, taking total solar capacity to 4 MW for captive use.
Supa began contributing in Q3 FY26 (October 1 onwards) at about 50-55% utilization in the first quarter; Q4 utilization rose further.
demand_pricing: Repeat revenue above 95% in FY26 from more than 120 domestic and global OEM customers; the business is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through.
Some large transformer clients are exploring multi-year supply agreements; management is evaluating the strategic and financial implications.
Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.
Management sees no demand deferment from domestic OEMs and no demand reduction from copper prices or the war; freight costs rose but were passed on on CIF basis.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Middle East impact on Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100-150 tons of dispatches slipped from March to April. Later, the estimated total effect including orders not started was 200-300 tons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per ton for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.question: Will payable days hold, and what is the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per ton differ between specialized and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard. The blended mix is expected to continue, with both segments growing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of exports and what drives the export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 30% of revenue, down from a high near 40%, and the target is to return to about 40% over the next couple of years. All exports go to T&D transformer OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for capacity beyond 59,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of demand deferment from domestic OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will transformer makers backward integrate into CTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

risks_watch: Working capital days stuck at 65-68 and operating cash flow negative in FY26 as receivables and inventory grew; payable-day gains depend on bank negotiations.
Middle East shipment timing and transport cost inflation, which can delay quarterly volumes.
Copper price moves distort reported margins even though EBITDA per ton is less affected.
EBITDA per ton could fall if standard wires grow faster than specialized wires, diluting the mix.
Supa Phase II timing (Q2 FY27 onward) and the ramp-up to 85% utilization taking 2-3 years.
New CTC entrants and imports, although management expects qualification to take 5-7 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, capacity and unit economics, with supporting numbers given for most questions. Management was more cautious and vague on EBITDA per ton and working capital, and declined to give CTC volume detail.
key_quotes: Specialized wire revenues overall also grew 103% YoY compared to 50 -60% growth in the prior two quarters.
So we expect that at least for FY27 our fixed cost will play out for the new capacity as it has played out in the last two quarters.
Now during Q4 FY26, we reported a quarterly record PAT of INR 34.5 crore, which increased 87% from Q4 of FY25.
This quarter, coppe r prices increased sharply, negatively impacting margins, but as you can see, did not impact EBITDA per ton.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth of at least FY26's 21%, backed by Supa Phase II taking installed capacity from 43,445 MT to about 59,000 MT (completion targeted FY27, contribution from around Q2 FY27) and 70% Q4 utilisation, though no order-book figures were given.
